draft.title: The 1967 and 2023 referendums
card: A referendum in 1967 asked voters to change the Constitution about First Nations people. It passed with a very large Yes vote.
First Nations people were to be counted in the census. The Commonwealth could also make laws for them, which it could not do before.
The Voice referendum asked whether to add an Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Voice, an advisory body, to the Constitution. It did not pass.
The 1967 change had wide support across parties. In 2023 the major parties were split, and the Yes vote did not win a national majority.
draft.remember: 1967 passed with wide support. The 2023 Voice referendum did not pass.

opts: It counted First Nations people and widened Commonwealth laws
It added a Voice to Parliament to the Constitution
It made Australia a republic with an elected president
It removed Commonwealth power to make laws for the states
a.why: The 1967 change counted First Nations people in the census and let the Commonwealth make laws for them. The Voice was the 2023 proposal, and it did not pass.
a.clue: Think of the census and who could make laws.

b.q: Which statement correctly compares the 1967 and 2023 referendums?
opts: 1967 passed, while 2023 did not pass
Both passed, but 2023 had a smaller Yes vote
Both failed to win a national majority
1967 did not pass, while 2023 passed
b.why: The 1967 referendum passed with a very large Yes vote. The 2023 Voice referendum did not pass. Reversing the two results is the common mistake.
b.clue: One result was a clear Yes and the other was a No.

problems.detail: 'The Commonwealth could also make laws for them, which it could not do before' overstates the change. Before 1967 the Commonwealth could already make laws for Aboriginal people in the territories, and its general laws applied to them. The 1967 change removed the words excluding 'the aboriginal race in any State' from the races power, so the Commonwealth could make special laws for First Nations people in the states. Better: 'could make special laws for First Nations people in the states'.

The right option says the referendum 'widened Commonwealth laws', which is vague. What changed was the Commonwealth's power to make laws for First Nations people, so 'widened Commonwealth law-making power' would be accurate.
